title: The spelling contest
text:
Rina had practised for two weeks. Every evening, her grandmother called out words, and Rina spelt them aloud. Now she stood on the stage of the school hall, and her hands felt cold.

"Your word is island," said the teacher. Rina took a deep breath. "Island. I-S-L-A-N-D. Island." The teacher smiled. "That is correct!"

Only Rina and a boy named Dimas were left. Dimas looked nervous too. The teacher gave Rina another word. "Necessary." Rina's mind went blank. Was it one c or two? One s or two? Then she remembered her grandmother's trick: one collar and two sleeves. One c and two s. "N-E-C-E-S-S-A-R-Y," she said slowly.

"Correct again!" said the teacher. Then Dimas spelt his word wrong, and Rina was the winner.

Rina did not shout or jump. First, she walked over to Dimas. "You spelt really well," she said. "I was lucky." Dimas grinned. Later, the two of them shared the prize, a big box of coloured pencils.
